item.title: The first time Namwali Serpell picked up ‘Beloved,’ she was baffled
item.description: Decades in the making, On Morrison is her breathtakingly comprehensive analysis of the Nobel laureate’s oeuvre.

item.title: Kadir Nelson on (and off) the court
item.description: The Caldecott Medalist’s latest illustrated slam dunk, Basket Ball, dives deep into the history of the beloved American sport.

item.title: Anna Kovatcheva’s vampire novel was born out of her lifelong obsessions
item.description: The debut author pulled from Bulgarian folklore, the gothic tradition and, of course, Buffy to create her unorthodox historical thriller.

item.title: Shelf Life with George Saunders: He’s always overcaffeinated
item.description: George Saunders, the inimitable author of Vigil, shares some of his favorite bookstore and library memories, and his feelings about “a simple coffee.”

item.title: The Hold List: Tuck in with 4 delectable titles
item.description: From simple snacks to elaborate banquets, food in all its forms has immense potential to spark connections between people. We’ve picked four books that explore this cornerstone of life in the tastiest of ways.

item.title: 5 titles with a major twist for ‘Stranger Things’ fans
item.description: Still reeling from the end of S5 and deep in #conformitygate? We get it, the hope will never die. While we wait for that secret episode that may never drop, here are 5 titles with satisfying twist endings we know you'll love.

item.title: 5 kaleidoscopic books for Black History Month
item.description: Our selections include a remembrance of the lost Tuskegee Airmen, an exploration of Coretta Scott King's activism, a history of Black History Month and more.

item.title: Few Blue Skies
item.description: In Carolina Ixta’s beautifully written tale of a girl who never stops pushing for a better future, she plants the seeds of advocacy, perseverance and hope.

item.title: Fros, Fades, and Braids
item.description: Throughout Fros, Fades, and Braids, Sean Qualls encourages young Black readers to fearlessly adopt their own sense of style and individuality.

item.title: Fustuk
item.description: Readers of Fustuk will be drawn to Robert Mgrdich Apelian’s art, stay for the magical joy throughout and walk away feeling full of familial love, but hungry for delicious food
